title: enterprise-migration-conversation-playbook-llm-apis
summary: A practical sales + solutions playbook for conversations where an enterprise is evaluating or actively migrating away from an existing LLM API provider. Focus: minimize risk, preserve feature parity, surface hidden costs and operational gaps, propose phased migration with clear fallbacks.
target_audience: AEs, SEs, Solutions Engineers, Customer Success managers working on renewal or migration opportunities from incumbent LLM API providers.
priority_messages: (1) Redwood gives predictable inference economics at scale (autoscaling + reserved pools + cost controls). (2) Same API and rollout semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private so customers avoid re-architecting. (3) Enterprise-grade controls: VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and compliance support. (4) Production runtime advantages: continuous batching, KV/prefix caching, and model fallback policies that reduce cost and improve availability.
discovery_questions: Avg request size (tokens), peak concurrency, latency SLOs, cold-start tolerance, on-prem / data residency needs, encryption & key management requirements, billing model tolerance (usage vs committed), eval sets for quality comparators, current failure modes and support pain points.
feature_matrix_highlights:
- Observability: token-level cost tracing and per-model latency heatmaps (Redwood).
- Rollouts: canary + automatic fallback to cheaper variants.
- Private option: full control plane in VPC + on-prem bundle.
- Runtime: continuous batching, KV cache, quantization-aware kernels.
- Pricing: commit/reserved + usage hybrid vs pure per-token inc. hidden egress on competitors.
(Use this section to map exact feature parity to the incumbent during calls.)
competitive_traps_to_watch_for:
- Competitor promises 'free' migration assistance but uses proprietary SDKs that lock customers in.
- Prospects focusing only on sticker price without considering tail latency and egress/execution costs.
- Engineers over-fixating on a single benchmark; real workloads differ in token distribution and concurrency.
- Claims of identical model behavior: small tokenization/decoder changes matter for hallucination-sensitive apps.
- 'We can do private hosting' -> check for control plane ownership, KMS support, and audit affordances.
objection_handling:
Objection: 'Your API is more expensive.' -> Response: break down unit economics: show token-level costing, effect of batching/caching, committed capacity discounts and an engagement model to run a short 'cost bake-off' with our Optimize team.
Objection: 'We need exact parity w/ current model outputs.' -> Response: propose a 3-week alignment sprint: side-by-side evals, prompt tuning, temperature/sampling parity checks and deterministic seeding for discrete outputs.
Objection: 'We can't change networking or cloud setup.' -> Response: highlight VPC-private control plane and on-prem option, plus stepwise migration with traffic mirroring.
Objection: 'We don't want vendor lock-in.' -> Response: emphasize model-agnostic API, open model catalog, and standard export of KV/cache and config (plus support for exporting deployment manifests).
talk_tracks_by_role: AE: focus on strategic outcomes (cost predictability, compliance). SE: bring technical checklist (token distribution, SLOs, cache-hit expectations). CSM: emphasize migration milestones and rollback policies. Engineering lead: propose performance benchmarks and integration plan; highlight kernel/quantization expertise and dedicated capacity options.
quick_play_actions: 1) Offer a non-production pilot: 2–4 week eval with representative traffic and a fixed sandbox budget. 2) Run automated cost comparison using customer's token traces (we provide a small script). 3) Propose a phased cutover: shadow traffic -> partial routing -> full routing with automatic model fallback. 4) Provide an SRE-run runbook for rollback and incident playbooks.
example_scenarios_and_snippets:
Scenario A (Regulated FinServ): customer worries about PII leakage and audit trails. Snippet: 'We will deploy a private control plane inside your VPC, integrate with your KMS, and provide token-level audit logs for 90/365 retention as required.'
Scenario B (Consumer chat product): worrying about per-message cost spikes. Snippet: 'We recommend prefix caching for frequent system prompts, and routing summary flows to a distilled model variant to reduce tokens while preserving UX.'
Scenario C (High-concurrency analytics): customer reports tail-latency spikes. Snippet: 'Dedicated reserved pools with configured burst capacity and continuous batching improves p95 by X ms in comparable deployments (share benchmark decks on request).'
migration_checklist:
- Export current token traces (7–14 days).
- Run Redwood 'cost-simulator' on traces.
- Identify prompt patterns eligible for prefix caching.
- Set up private control plane / VPC access if required.
- Run side-by-side quality evals on 500 representative prompts.
- Create rollback and monitoring playbook (SLOs, error budgets, fallback models).
- Agree on SLA, committed capacity, and escalation contacts.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: unexpected quality delta after model switch -> Mitigation: canary to subset of users + prompt tuning + auto-fallback.
Risk: temporary latency regressions -> Mitigation: enable burst capacity and tune batching windows, instrument p50/p95/p99.
Risk: hidden costs during migration -> Mitigation: pilot budget with precise usage alerts and daily cost dashboards.
closing_checklist_for_deal:
- Legal: confirm data residency and KMS terms.
- Finance: finalize committed capacity and billing cadence.
- Security: run pen-test and confirm logging retention.
- Ops: validate cutover runbook and monitoring hooks.
- Exec sponsor: sign-off on migration timeline and measurable success criteria.
